name: Exception Handling Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in exception handling work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in exception handling work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Surface known limitations of a chosen exception handling approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
2. When exception handling guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Prefer explicit, readable exception handling solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
4. When multiple exception handling strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
5. Before starting exception handling work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
6. Validate exception handling outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to exception handling (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated exception handling concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new exception handling abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting exception handling assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of exception handling correctness.
- Do not silently drop exception handling edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about exception handling over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
